subject: Helios Health — private hosting discovery & prioritized risks
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Alex Roman <alex.r@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Helios Health — initial post-call recap: private hosting constraints and top priorities

Alex / team — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and can move to scheduling the technical deep dive with your infra lead. I tried to capture the pain, goals, and the constraints you emphasized. Please correct any inaccuracies.

Summary of pain & goals
- Data residency / regulatory driver: patient PII and billing data must remain within US regions; Helios requires SOC 2 and audit logs retained for 3 years.
- Network isolation: preference for a VPC-hosted/private control plane; potential air-gapped option for some workloads (research exports) depending on compliance review.
- Latency & predictable throughput: primary production workloads must hit 150ms median token latency target at peak traffic (we discussed burst windows).
- Cost sensitivity: procurement will need estimated committed capacity pricing and a clear uplift for air-gapped or private deployments.

Top technical constraints called out by your team
1) No outbound internet egress from the processing subnet — all outbound must go via a NAT/proxy controlled by Helios.
2) TLS termination requirement at customer edge; Redwood must support mutual TLS and certificate rotation via your KMS/HSM.
3) IP allowlist only — no DNS-based routing for control plane endpoints.
4) KV/cache persistence must be configurable to avoid persisting PHI to shared storage.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA)
- Nikhil: share a concise hosting pre-reqs doc and a 1-pager checklist (attached). ACTION: sent in this thread.
- Alex: provide your IT point of contact and an initial network diagram (requested as attachment in next reply). DUE: EOD Thu 8/1.
- Marissa: coordinate a 60-minute technical deep-dive for your infra team + ours (suggested slots linked). OWNER: Marissa.
- Monica: draft a scoped quote & high-level SOW for Dedicated/private hosting options, including an air-gap add-on. OWNER: Monica. DELIVERABLE: first pass by 8/4.

Attachments included with this email
- redwood_vpc_prereqs.pdf (PDF) — short checklist of IPs, TLS/KMS requirements, and allowed egress patterns.
- redwood_onepager_hosting_checklist.pdf (PDF) — one-page summary for your procurement team.

Questions / open items
- Which subset of traffic (token streams) must be air-gapped vs allowed to use private egress? This will determine whether we need physical air-gapped packaging.
- Do you have an internal SLA floor (p95 or p99 targets) that we should map to our Dedicated offering?

Thanks — I’ll leave scheduling to Marissa but happy to coordinate directly with your IT lead.

Best,

-- 
Nikhil Sharma
Solution Engineer, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood_vpc_prereqs.pdf, redwood_onepager_hosting_checklist.pdf]

From: Alex Roman <alex.r@helioshealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helioshealth.com, it_lead@helioshealth.com
Date: Wed, 1 Aug 2028 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Helios Health — initial post-call recap: private hosting constraints and top priorities

Thanks, Nikhil — this is helpful and mostly accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

Corrections / clarifications
- The 3-year audit log retention is required for billing records only; other telemetry can be 12 months.
- For the air-gap ask: it applies only to model training outputs and any export containing full billing histories. Real-time inference can remain within a private VPC with no public egress.

Action items from Helios
- Procurement will review your 1-pager and respond re: committed capacity structure. CCing procurement.
- IT (copied) — please coordinate with Nikhil & Marissa on the network diagram and confirm whether site-to-site VPN or direct connect is preferred.

Attachments to follow: we will send a first-pass network diagram (PDF) and our internal compliance checklist for SOC 2 items — expect by EOD Thu.

Also: we’ll need a sample SOW to expedite approvals — procurement asked for a redlined draft. Can you share a base SOW?

Appreciate the recap — looking forward to the deep dive.

— Alex
Alex Roman
VP Finance & Operations, Helios Health
alex.r@helioshealth.com

Marissa / Monica — forwarding Alex’s confirmation. Two tactical items before the tech deep-dive:

1) Tech deep-dive scope (60 min) — proposed agenda
   - 10m: introductions and goal alignment (Helios infra, security owners + Redwood infra leads)
   - 15m: network topology review (Helios network diagram + Redacted Redwood control-plane endpoints)
   - 15m: auth & certs (mTLS, rotations, KMS/HSM integration options)
   - 10m: data handling & KV/cache persistence options (ensure no PHI leak to shared storage)
   - 10m: next steps & decision log (what requires legal/procurement vs engineering)

2) Pre-req checklist for IT (please review the attached redwood_vpc_prereqs.pdf) — must confirm:
   - Which of the two connectivity options: site-to-site VPN OR direct connect / private link?
   - Specific outbound proxy/FW egress constraints (we can support NAT/proxy patterns but need the configuration example).
   - KMS integration pattern: do you want us to call your KMS for envelope keys or to manage keys on Redwood with imported wrapping keys?

Suggested deep-dive slots (links below) — Marissa, can you pick and send invites + a short agenda to Alex & IT?
- Thu 8/2: 11:00–12:00 PT
- Fri 8/3: 09:00–10:00 PT
- Fri 8/3: 14:00–15:00 PT

Monica — I captured procurement’s ask for a base SOW / redline. I attached a starting SOW we can use; please produce a scoped quote that separates Dedicated VPC pricing and an air-gap packaging add-on.

Thanks — I’ll join the deep-dive.
